text:
maria.support: FYI, customer acme-corp reporting large number of 5xx errors (502/504) to hosted inference API /v1/generate starting ~2026-03-15T10:10Z. They see ~60% failures, sample IDs attached. They say it started suddenly after a deploy window.
maria.support: I ran basic repro from my laptop -> intermittent TLS handshake timeouts. Example:
```
$ curl -v 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>'
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
*   Trying 34.120.45.67...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to api.redwood.example (34.120.45.67) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake timeout
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) OpenSSL SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to api.redwood.example:443 
```
maria.support: Customer ticket: TKT-4592. I'm escalating — they are hitting production traffic and want ETA.
ops-bot: alert: edge-proxy-us-east TLS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT spike at 2026-03-15T10:11:23Z (5xx rate 58% -> page sent)
kevin.cloudops: @maria.support can you paste a full s_client output and the trace IDs from the customer logs? need to know if this is client->edge or edge->origin. also which region (us-east?)
maria.support: sending s_client and a tcpdump snippet. Region: us-east-1. Trace IDs: 0a3f7, 0a3f8, 0a3f9.
```
$ openssl s_client -connect api-us-east.redwood.net:443 -servername api.redwood.example -timeout 5
CONNECTED(00000003)
140735...:error:14077410:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:sslv3 alert handshake failure:ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:1523
---
No peer certificate available
---
SSL handshake has read 0 bytes and written 317 bytes
---
``` 
maria.support: tcpdump shows client SYN, SYN-ACK, then TLS ClientHello, no ServerHello within ~3s for affected flows.
jenna.infra: I'm seeing an odd correlation with our cert-roll service that ran at 10:05Z. ACME rotation job started, attempted to fetch new certs and update edge nodes. Some nodes logged DNS resolution errors when contacting the CA/validation endpoints. suspect DNS resolver flakiness in the forwarder cluster -> intermittent failures cause edge to serve stale/partial cert state leading to handshake failures.
kevin.cloudops: can you paste the resolver errors? which forwarders? provider? any SERVFAIL/REFUSED?
jenna.infra: logs (filtered):
```
2026-03-15T10:05:11Z resolver-01 forwarder: lookup ca-validation.acme.local -> SERVFAIL
2026-03-15T10:05:11Z resolver-02 forwarder: lookup ca-validation.acme.local -> timeout
2026-03-15T10:05:12Z cert-rotate: node edge-23 update -> failed to fetch cert (dns lookup failed)
```
jenna.infra: our telemetry shows increased DNS latency from our forwarders to upstream provider X at 10:04-10:07Z (p99 > 2s). that matches the customer window. when cert refresh fails some nodes fall back to in-memory previous cert which in some cases was expired for the SNI name in client request -> TLS alert and 502/504 manifested.
sam.runtime: that's consistent with the trace IDs — the edge logs show TLS alert 40 (handshake failure) and then connection close. looks like client initiated SNI for api.redwood.example but server didn't have matching cert because rotation was only partially applied.
kevin.cloudops: good catch. next steps: 1) roll back the cert-rotation (force previous cert to all edges), 2) fail ACME job until we resolve upstream resolver provider, 3) rotate DNS forwarders to 1.1.1.1/8.8.8.8 as a temporary mitigation, 4) add customer credit for outage window, 5) open an incident and page eng-runtime and infra (already done).
maria.support: started a manual rollback of certs to the previous bundle on affected edge nodes (edge-21..edge-30) at 10:17Z per runbook, will monitor.
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-1276 (severity: high) — oncall: @sam.runtime, @jenna.infra, @kevin.cloudops
jenna.infra: I also opened a ticket with upstream DNS provider (PRV-9921) — they reported partial peering flap in us-east region during 10:03-10:09Z.
kevin.cloudops: can we confirm recovery metrics? Maria, any customer confirmation?
maria.support: after rollback finished at 10:20Z error rate dropped from 58% -> 2% within ~2 minutes. customer confirmed in ticket: "we're back, thanks". I issued a goodwill credit (billing note attached) and updated the customer.
sam.runtime: engineering follow-up: add stronger retries around cert fetch, mark ACME job to use multiple resolvers in parallel, add alerting on partial-certificate state (when some edges have new cert and others not). filing follow-up RFC.
maria.support: I'll close the customer ticket after attaching incident summary and RCA once available. thanks all. :thumbsup:
kevin.cloudops: arch note for postmortem: root cause = upstream DNS resolver peering flap during cert rotation window -> partial cert deployment -> TLS handshake failures -> 5xx for client traffic. mitigation = rollback + multi-resolver + provider ticket + monitoring.
sam.runtime: adding follow-up actions to INC-2026-1276 and will coordinate a scheduled cert-rotation retry after resolver fix.
jenna.infra: logging note: saving tcpdumps and edge cert metadata for the RCA bundle (attached to INC-2026-1276).
maria.support: closing thread here, moving updates to the incident."
